title: Support query params in st.page_link
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Reading an writing query params using [`st.query_params`](https://<redacted-host>/library/api-reference/utilities/st.query_params) can be quire useful. It would be handy to support passing query params with [`st.page_link`](https://<redacted-host>/library/api-reference/widgets/st.page_link)

### Why?

Useful for creating drill down page links, and improves sharing a page's state using the url.

### How?

* introduce a new parameter `query_params: dict[str, str | Iterable[str]]` to `st.page_link` to attach query params to the link: `st.page_link(page="pages/foo.py", query_params={"my": "params", "go": "here"})`
* and/or allow query params in the `page` argument: `st.page_link(page="pages/foo.py?my=params&go=here")`

### Additional Context

_No response_

comments.body:
Cool idea! Thanks for the contribution and starting a PR.

Should it work for `st.switch_page()` too? Although technically I think that's possible today by setting some session_state before switching the page and then updating query_params based on it afterwards.

I want to think about this and discuss about the API with a couple members of the Streamlit team. @reporter in case you want to wait for a final decision from the team about this new API before investing too much more time into it.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
So I was actually trying to make a step in a direction where I can use query params as sharable page state. Creating links with query params is just a convenience that fits in that workflow. If that's not how steamlit is supposed to work I understand.

The broader idea I was trying to get working is that it would be cool to be able to just grab the url, send it to someone, and bring their page in the same state.

Something like this doesn't work, but you'll get the idea:
```python
import streamlit as st

# set default value
value = 5

# override with query params value, if set
value = int(st.query_params.get("value", value))

# show widget
value = st.slider(min_value=0, max_value=10, value=value, label="foo")
# update query params, so the url represents the page's sharable state
st.query_params["value"] = value

# do awesome stuff
...

```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Great! Yeah that use case makes sense. It's definitely a common one and something we want to make easier over time.

By the way, it should be possible to do something similar to what you described today using query_params + session_state with a key arg on the slider to link to session_state.

There's another similar feature I'd love to support for "binding" a given widget value to session state and query param value as a single API call or argument, so it's even simpler than today. Hoping we can get to that in the next few months.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
`switch_page` does actually send the current query params with the rerun data:

```
ctx.script_requests.request_rerun(
        RerunData(
            query_string=ctx.query_string,
            page_script_hash=matched_pages[0]["page_script_hash"],
        )
    )
```

But @participant1 I think the current behavior is to throw that string away when a page switch is detected. So either that behavior would need to change, this function would need a special injection point for the new query string in the rerun data that doesn't get discarded.

Page_link is different bc it's handled by the frontend; page link proto would need an update to store query params and then apply them to the rerun data like above.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi all, Streamlit team discussed and we're happy to see this added.

```python
st.page_link("pages/settings.py", query_params={"update_pwd": True})
st.switch_page("pages/dashboard.py", query_params={"team": "streamlit"})
```

- Ideally we would add it to both together for consistency.
- Takes dict input
- We should handle dict values the same way we do when setting values in st.query_params
    - e.g. set multiple values when passing list
    - best effort try to convert things to str()
    - (Ideally it goes through literally the same code path for consistency)

If anyone wants to take a crack at it (maybe picking up from @reporter 's work in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/8115 or if you want to keep going!) including some unit tests, it's welcome and we can review and shepherd. Otherwise we'll get to it as someone has cycles to pick it up :)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
And I will add to this, it's probably a good idea to special-case passing `st.query_params` to the new keyword argument such that it goes through the `get_all` pathway instead of normal `_getitem_` calls.

That way, you can use `st.switch_page("page2.py", query_params=st.query_params)` to switch to a new page and keep _all_ the current params, even if there are ones with multiple values.

As I was working through this, I'm not so sure it makes sense to add this to `switch_page`; the reason being that the following two bits of code would be functionally identical:
```python
st.switch_page("my_page_2", query_params={"foo": "bar", "baz": [1, 2, 3]})
# AND 
st.query_params.from_dict({"foo": "bar", "baz": [1, 2, 3]})
st.switch_page("my_page_2")
```
So there's really no need for the extra keyword argument there, @participant1. It's useful on `page_link` because the page change is triggered by a user there so you need to encode those query params on the front-end.

Hey @participant2 
Great that you're taking a swing at this!!

The issue https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8102 explains why it would also be useful for `switch_page`.
I was trying to make a page_switch while also passing parameters. This way, after the switch page, if the user were to refresh the page in the browser, the query parameters would still be in the URL.

It's been I while since I looked at this, so I gave 
```
st.query_params.from_dict({"foo": "bar", "baz": [1, 2, 3]})
st.switch_page("my_page_2")
```
a try again and it seems, I guess as expected, that the query parameters disappear (at least from the browser URL) after the switch_page.

I tried it the other way around before as well (see issue https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8102), but that doesn't give exactly the expected beheaviour:
> While the same result could be achieved by two consecutive calls - one to st.switch_page, followed by a call to st.query_params - this will cause the browser (Chrome at least) to keep two steps in history. As such, the back-button would not return to the page before the st.page_switch but instead to the page after the switch without query parameters.

I'm a bit rusty on the details, so please let me know if I'm missing something here.

@participant4 I think you found a bug! This is interesting: my suggestion _does_ seem to persist the params across the page change, however the front-end seems to be removing them from the URL:
![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/5677417/edf5fb33-21d0-4263-94b7-287ff899652b)

This is seemingly just a problem with switch_page in the _current_ version of streamlit (1.36.0), and is not caused by my changes.

```python
# in main.py
import streamlit as st

st.query_params.from_dict({"bar": "foo"})
if st.button("switch"):
    st.switch_page("pages/a.py")

# in pages/a.py
import streamlit as st

st.write("QueryParams: ", st.query_params)
```

And, yeah, I think that's the reason why it's still useful to have query_params kwarg in st.switch_page. I think this happens because - when performing a switch_page first (with session_state variables stored) and then query_params (updating the URL based on session_state variables) - these are seen as two "previous steps" by the browser.

Just checking in on this, seems like we lost some momentum unfortunately. I think my use case is a bit different - I'm able to carry query params around between pages using session state and `st.query_params` but that doesn't work if a user opens a link in a new tab (session state is cleared). So carrying state through to the new page doesn't work, and since there's no way to append query params to the link (whether navigation `Page` or `page_link`), we can't carry state that way either.

The only solutions I could think of would be to use a cookies component or to maybe manually add the links via HTML.. but those don't sound like great ideas.

## Update

Support for passing query params to `st.page_link` will be released in 1.52:

```python
st.page_link(..., query_params={"hello": "world", "foo": ["bar", "baz"]}
```
